card.solution: Disorganized sewage management poses one of the most significant threats to the natural environment. It results in pollution of soil, surface waters, and groundwater, primarily. The Solina Commune faces a significant challenge due to the lack of complete sewage infrastructure in the communes's constituent localities. The failure to construct sewage systems leads to further environmental degradation of an extent and scope that are difficult to ascertain. Conversely, the state of the water supply network in Skhidnytsia is very poor, with over 50% of the water supply network being overused and in a constant state of emergency. Drinking water losses during transport and distribution in this network average around 70%. The overall goal of the project is the protection and enhancement of the natural environment, including water resources, through effective wastewater management. This objective will be achieved through the following specific goals: - Reducing environmental pollution by developing wastewater infrastructure and improving wastewater management practices. - Minimizing water losses from water supply systems and enhancing the rational use of water. - Increasing residents' ecological awareness regarding reservoir protection, particularly water resources, and promoting their sustainable management within the project area. Promoting sustainable water resource management, including wastewater management, and collaborative actions aimed at protecting and enhancing these resources are crucial for several significant reasons: - Ensuring access to clean water. - Protecting aquatic ecosystems. - Minimizing the impact of climate change. - Avoiding water conflicts. - Sustainable economic development. The main scope of the project: 1) Construction of a sanitary sewerage network (6,9971 km) with the necessary technical infrastructure for the village of Werlas in the Solina Commune (28 households (approximately 106 people), 1 public facility and 5 businesses connected). 2) Reconstruction of 3,7km of water pipeline in Skhidnytsia (435 private subscribers will be connected(2 600) ppl, as well as 27 businesses and public facilities). 3) Three-day ecological workshops focused on environmental protection and water conservation are planned for the youth from the Solina Commune (20 participants) and the Skhidnytsia Community (20 participants), aged 14-15 years. 4) Two ecological project conferences will be organized for representatives of local authorities, environmental non-governmental organizations, nature conservation institutions, and youth representatives. 5) Production of a promotional film titled "Water's Trail", focusing on the conservation of water resources and their sustainable recreational use. The purpose of the project is to enhance cooperation through the exchange of good practices based on the implementation of sustainable development principles. The main benefits of the initiative include the protection and safeguarding against pollution of locally flowing rivers and groundwater. From a cross-border perspective, the investment in the Solina commune is also significant for residents of western Ukraine. The hydroisohip map indicates that within river alluvia in the Podkarpackie Voivodeship in Poland, groundwater flow follows the course of rivers. This suggests that cross-border flows from Poland to Ukraine are possible, allowing pollutants to penetrate groundwater across the border. The consequences for the environment can be irreversible and exacerbate residents' comfort and health conditions.

card.solution: Both partners share the common element of transboundary rivers. Effective protection of these rivers requires joint and coordinated investment actions on both sides of the border. meta.title: Clean water - development of sustainable water management in the transboundary area.

card.solution: Water is a limited and vulnerable resource - essential for life and development. For many decades, the key tasks of water management were exclusively concerned with the use and technological utilisation of water. However, progressive climate change is strongly affecting both environmental resources and needs. Adaptation measures that also take into account land-use planning solutions are therefore necessary, and one of the key resources in this process is water. Proper management of its resources is therefore particularly important. The described phenomena have intensified strongly in the last few decades and cause negative effects, which are also a serious problem in the Polish-Ukrainian cross-border area. Particularly noticeable are the increases in temperatures that cause periods of drought which translates into water shortages. Although overall water consumption in most of the cross-border area has decreased in recent years, there are still shortcomings in terms of sewerage network coverage and availability of clean water. The population, especially in Ukraine, is often connected to an inefficient and outdated public water supply network, resulting in both water losses and a deterioration of drinking water quality. On the Polish side, the situation looks better, although there are cases, especially in rural areas, where entire villages are not connected to the sewage system. The current situation is due to infrastructural shortcomings, manifested in an underdeveloped sewage and water supply network and low awareness among residents and public institutions. The diagnosed problems are also related to the project area, where in the Bukowsko commune the village of Dudyńce does not have a sewage system, as a result of which the environment (especially streams) is polluted through leaking septic tanks and sometimes residents pouring sewage directly onto fields or into streams, which are then transferred to the San River. This situation is also due to a lack of awareness on the part of residents that well-treated sewage can be reused in nature in the form of water. More broadly, this problem relates to a lack of knowledge on how to manage water sensibly, especially in times of climate change. On the Ukrainian side in Rudky, the village centre lacks a functioning sewage network and individual septic tanks do not meet sanitary requirements. The old sewage network infrastructure is highly degraded and disused due to lack of public funds for modernisation and expansion. The leakage of sewage into the ground poses a high sanitary and environmental risk as it then finds its way into the Wysznia River and then into the San River. As a result of the project, the level of development of sustainable water management in the transboundary area in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town will increase. The length of the sewerage infrastructure will increase by 4,086 metres on the Polish side and 2,513 metres on the Ukrainian side and there will be an improvement in wastewater management in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town. Rainwater storage and reuse infrastructure will be developed in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town. In the Municipality of Bukowsko, two rain gardens will be constructed in the villages of Dudyńce and Pobiedno. In the Town of Rudky, a reservoir will be created to collect rainwater and then use it for firefighting. The level of awareness of residents about the water cycle and the need for water management in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town will be increased through participation in workshops and conferences.

meta.title: Cross-border development of water supply and sewerage system - Good Water Tyczyn - Pustomyty
meta.institution: Municipal Utilities Company "Eko-Strug" Limited Liability Company

card.solution: The common goal and the expected change is to improve the quality of residents’ lifes and adapting Tyczyn (TM) and Pustomyty (PST) to changing climatic conditions by increasing the availability of good water and protecting the natural environment of the borderland from pollution through the development of the sewage system. Poland (SDG report 2022) has very poor renewable freshwater resources (1600 m³/person/year). This is one of the lowest values in the EU (3 times less than average). The situation in UA is even worse - 1240 m³/person (State Water Resources Agency - 2019). According to the UN, less than 1700 m³ means water security threat.The most important problems diagnosed in the border area include underdeveloped water/sewage infrastructure which negatively affects the environmental, social and economic spheres. The low degree of water supply (about 66% in TM and 53% in PST) and sewerage (62% in TM and 35% in PST) adversely affects not only the comfort of life, but also the level of sanitary safety, as the risk of gastrointestinal diseases increases, due to the consumption of water with undetermined parameters, mainly by the uncoordinated creation of domestic water intakes (wells), as well as through the large number of domestic septic tanks (which cause groundwater contamination through leaks). Both cities have become convenient places for settlement, as they are adjacent to large and important urban centers (PST = Lviv, TM = Rzeszow). This has an impact on the steady population/clients growth (TM: 10,499 people in 2019 to 11,397 in 2022; PST: 2019 - 20,410 clients to 20,604 in 2022), which translates into increases in water consumption and more wastewater. Insufficiently developed and often outdated water/sewage infrastructure isn’t able to meet these challenges, that’s why significant increases in failures have been observed (TM own data for water: 2019 - 15 failures, 2022 - 20 failures = 33% increase + sewerage 18 and 23 respectively = 27.8% increase) and in PST (own data for water: 2019 - 32 failures, 2022 - 79 failures = 146.9% increase + sewerage 98 and 312 respectively = 218.4% increase). The ongoing war in UA also has had a significant impact on the catastrophic changes in access to water. The investment is of strategic importance for the border provinces (Rzeszow and Lviv), which also face the problem of inadequate amount of water for supplying residents during periods of drought (and due to the ongoing war). The well-developed networks belonging to the Partners can also serve as an emergency water supply for these cities. PL/UA common challenges: droughts/climate changes, water supply interruptions and/or significant reductions in water pressure, environmental pollution due to lack of sewerage, increasing number of failures, low awareness of residents about the need to save water. In response to the above, the partners identified the main objectives of the project as: - Increase availability and ensure good quality water for newly connected 210 Poles and 3544 Ukrainians (+3923, which are already connected to this pipeline) through the construction of new water pipeline PL-3,8 km, UA-1,2 km. - protecting the environment through the development of an improved public sewage system: PL – 2,76 km (connecting 207 Poles) and by modernizing sewage system for 7361 Poles and 6731Ukrainians. - Adaptation to changes by increasing awareness of saving and obtaining drinking water in emergency situations among 1200 Poles and Ukrainians A cross-border approach is necessary, as both partners have different experiences, thanks to the exchange of which (by joint training, creation of joint procedures – 10 PL/UA employees) the UA partner will gain the necessary knowledge on modern solutions and technologies used in water and sewage systems and the PL partner will gain knowledge on how to respond more effectively in crisis and critical situations. The above will benefit the residents of TM, PST - indirectly also Lviv and Rzeszów

meta.title: New historical life of Wiśniowiec and Tarnobrzeg parks

card.solution: Cross-border restoration project of historic parks in Tarnobrzeg (Poland) and Wiśniowiec (Ukraine) and assessment of their ecosystem value in terms of historical development is aimed at improving the condition of the environment, strengthening the protection and preservation of landscape monuments (objects of the nature reserve fund), biodiversity of green infrastructure in urban areas and reducing pollution. The project aims to popularize the value of park plantings for the environment (urboecosystem). As part of this project, it is planned to carry out joint research of the vegetation cover of two parks (Ukrainian and Polish), quantitative and cost indicators of their ecosystem services and development of proposals for improving the ecological condition of facilities and their dissemination. The overriding goal of the project is meeting the recreational, cultural, educational and environmental needs of the residents of the housing estates (Ukrainian and Polish) with the expected increase in environmental awareness of park visitors. The main objective of the project is to improve the ecological condition of historic parks in the border regions of Poland and Ukraine - in Tarnobrzeg and Wiśniowiec, to assess the general condition of the parks in terms of development and implementation of recommendations regarding the improvement of the condition of green areas and their ecological functions. To achieve this goal, the following main directions have been set: - developing a concept for the development/restoration of urban landscapes; - measurement of biometric indicators of trees and shrubs; - determination of quantitative and valuable indicators of ecological functions of trees in terms of their ability to reduce the environmental pollution, carbon sequestration, oxygen production and regulation of the water flow; - analysis of the information received in terms of various ecosystem services, categories of green areas and species composition; - presentation of the information received in the form of an interactive map; - developing possibilities and prospects for presenting the obtained results to local authorities, interested persons and organizations; - implementation of the proposed actions to improve the ecological and aesthetic condition of parks and increasing their ecosystem value. As a result of the project implementation, the following is expected: 1. Preparation of applications regarding the condition of parks and their green areas; 2. Quantitative and qualitative assessment of ecosystem services of two parks; 3. Recommendations for improving the sanitary, aesthetic and ecosystem condition of parks; 4. Ecological effect from the implementation of measures to improve the condition of parks and to increase their ecosystem value; 5. Preservation of the common natural and cultural heritage of Ukraine and Poland; 6. Sustainable use of environmentally valuable areas; 7. Dissemination of experience in the implementation of projects for the protection of landscape monuments - historical parks (organization of a scientific and practical conference, development of methodological recommendations); 8. Raising the ecological awareness of the inhabitants of the nearby housing estates and people visiting the facilities. The main beneficiaries of the project are scientists/researchers of historic parks and biodiversity of objects in Poland and Ukraine, residents of Tarnobrzeg and Wiśniowiec, especially young people, Eco-activists and park visitors. meta.title: Urban Lungs – Smart Green Infrastructure Solutions for Urbanized Communities in Poland and Ukraine.

card.solution: Project acronym: UrbanLungs. The project covers the suburbs of the city of Jarosław - town of Wysocko and Pawłosiów in the District of Jarosław in Poland and the city of Uzhhorod in Zakarpattia Oblast of Ukraine. It is addressing the problem described in Specific Objective 1.3 - "Strengthening the protection and conservation of nature, biodiversity and green infrastructure", including urban areas, and reducing all forms of pollution. This is an ambitious plan aimed at reducing rate of pollution, which opens a new chapter of improving of green zones in the project territory. The overall objective of the project is to improve existing and create new urban green areas in the border regions of Poland and Ukraine through the elaboration of scientifically based concepts for revitalization and development of green areas in urban communities in line with the EU standards and climate change responding concepts based on 4 pilot projects in Uzhhorod territorial community and DistrictJaroslaw . The project objectives include the development of scientifically based concepts for the development of green urban areas, the revitalization of 3 existing and the creation of 1 new green zone, as well as the dissemination of best practices and project recommendations among other 75 (64 UA and 11 PL) municipalities in the Zakarpattia Oblast and Podkarpackie Voivodeship. Addressing these challenges requires an integrated approach and the participation of experts in the fields of ecology, biology, landscape design, urbanism, public engagement and sustainable development. It also involves ongoing cooperation with local communities, government agencies and other stakeholders to ensure the success and sustainability of the project. The project will produce reports on the impact of green spaces on pollution and the environment in the cities of Uzhhorod, Wysocko and Pawlosiów, an environmental inventory of green spaces in Tetiana Park in Uzhhorod, a dendrological inventory and a concept for the development of the territory of the Manor and Palace Complex in Pawłosiów and the Palace and Park Complex in Wysocko, as well as recommendations for increasing and/or reviving green spaces for urban communities in the border areas of Poland and Ukraine developed in the course of the project implementation on the basis of scientifically sound concepts. In addition, a number of educational activities will be held for students and secondary school pupils who want to study ecology and urbanism, as well as develop their analytical, critical and practical skills. As a result of the scientific and practical conference, a collection of conference materials, joint methodological recommendations developed based on the results of the research will be published, and a cross-border forum on the importance of implementing green space policy for the sustainable development of border communities in Ukraine and Poland will become a platform for creating a memorandum of cooperation between representatives of Polish and Ukrainian communities and developing a joint algorithm of actions to improve the condition of green areas on the ground. By focusing on the restoration and expansion of green areas in towns and the development of scientifically based methods for revitalizing green spaces, the project not only improves the environmental condition of cities, but also contributes to the creation of a healthy and harmonious environment for communities. The project will unite the strong Ukraininan scientific and pracical expertise in ecology and environmental sciences with Polish experience and knowledge in green zone planning in line with European standarts, that will allow to produce best solutions for PL-UA green infrastructure together with its implementation in practice. It will create not only new partners link at different levels but long-term cross-border effects on reduce air polution in the borderzone.

meta.title: THE CARPATHIAN NARROW-GAUGE RAILWAYS - A JOURNEY IN THE FOOTSTEPS OF THE CARPATHIAN FOREST RAILWAYS
meta.institution: FOUNDATION OF THE BIESZCZADY FOREST RAILWAY

card.solution: The project focuses on two areas in the Eastern Carpathians, associated with the history and location of preserved historical forest narrow-gauge railways in Majdan (PL) and Vyhoda (UA). For both areas, the history of narrow-gauge railways and the potential utilization of this heritage represent a significant but underutilized tourism potential. One of the main challenges of this project is the INSUFFICIENT USE OF THE TOURIST POTENTIAL FOR LOCAL SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. As a result, both areas experience economic stagnation, an aging population (high youth migration, negative birth rate), and often unemployment. Tourism development presents a great opportunity, and therefore, innovative actions need to be taken to increase the average length of stay and tourism revenues. To achieve this, both areas need to implement innovative measures and expand, enhance, and integrate their offerings through cross-border cooperation. The overall objective of the project is to increase the role of tourism based on the endogenous historical and cultural potential in the development of Polish-Ukrainian border areas in the Eastern Carpathians. The expected changes that the project will bring about include: - Facilitating cooperation and exchange of experience between project partners and surrounding communities in cross-border areas to develop and promote a common, integrated offer of sustainable tourism. - Expanding and enhancing the offerings of project partners. - Creating a cohesive image by equipping public spaces and narrow-gauge railway station areas in Majdan and Vyhoda in a way that enhances the quality of these places as tourist attractions while respecting their history and the value of the surrounding nature. These changes will be achieved through investment and soft measures implemented in the project, such as building innovative infrastructure for the Bieszczady Forest Railway Station in Majdan, introducing alternative forms of pro-ecological railway and bicycle transport in the Eastern Carpathians, developing visitor infrastructure and walking/cycling routes along the Vyhoda heritage railway route, joint familiarization visits to present an integrated joint tourist offer with the Carpathian Forest Railways logo to travel bloggers and tour operators, cross-border workshops on creating a common integrated tourist offer and joint cross-border festivals promoting local heritage and tourism attractions. The main target groups of the project include institutions related to cultural heritage, operators of tourist attractions, and tourism service providers (approximately 20 entities), travel bloggers, and tourism operators from Ukraine and Poland, local development agencies (3 entities), and representatives of local and regional authorities (6 entities). The project will involve approximately 1,070 participants. The ultimate beneficiaries are enthusiasts of narrow-gauge railways, tourists, residents, and entrepreneurs from the project areas (approximately 140,000 in PL and 80,000 in UA). From a cross-border perspective, both target areas face the challenge of harnessing the untapped economic potential of cross-border tourism by offering visitors a joint tourist offer that includes a cross-border trip to the neighbouring historical railways still in operation in the Eastern Carpathians. Currently, there is a lack of cooperation, joint marketing, and exchange of tourists between partners. This is further exacerbated by a lack of information about tourist attractions, services, and accommodations, leading to a lack of awareness among tourists about the attractions they can experience on the other side of the border. The project will enable both areas to access visitors and tourists from the other side of the border and enter the cross-border tourism market with a joint offer that integrates more diversified and meaningful holiday experiences within a single trip to the heritage railways.

meta.title: Cooperation beyond borders - Small Projects Fund on the Polish-Ukrainian border.

card.solution: The current cross-border cooperation on the Polish-Ukrainian border between various entities from the public sector, civil society, and primarily residents, is not very intensive. It is based primarily on contacts and relations established over the years, which have rather limited scope and potential, considering the vast area covered by the Programme and the current situation in Ukraine. A new impetus and bottom-up initiatives are needed to achieve the goal of promoting and supporting the establishment of new contacts, relationships, and initiatives at the interpersonal level, in order to achieve long-term cooperation. Taking such actions will help to significantly increase trust and establish new interpersonal relations among the residents of the Programme area. Additionally, it should be emphasized that the Russian invasion of Ukraine has significantly changed and limited the cooperation between institutions and residents of the border region, thereby requiring additional measures to address new challenges. The war and its consequences have had a profound impact on the situation in the Ukrainian part of the Programme area. It has also caused an unprecedented influx of refugees to Poland. The response to these needs and challenges is the implementation of the SPF, the main objective of which is to build mutual trust, in particular by encouraging interpersonal activities through the implementation of small projects. The specific objectives of the SPF include: - increasing the use of cultural/natural heritage and the development of education, integration of border residents and building mutual trust and good neighbourly relations. The achievement of this project objective will be achieved through the implementation and execution of small cross-border projects and shall directly translate into achieving the objective of the Programme in the field of supporting cross-border development processes at the border of Poland and Ukraine, and it will also enable the achievement of product and result indicators assigned to the SPF. Small projects implemented in the Polish-Ukrainian border region are directly aimed at the residents of the border area, thereby serving the local community, activating it for cooperation, strengthening contacts, as well as building and reinforcing a common identity. Small projects will primarily focus on: Integration of residents of the Programme area in the field of arts and culture; - Cross-border cooperation in the field of education; - Integration and capacity-building initiatives in the field of health and safety; Eligible activities shall include: - organizing events and initiatives involving the target audience in joint cultural and creative leisure activities, joint actions by cultural and artistic institutions, as well as cross-border NGOs; - joint protection and promotion of cultural and artistic heritage; - joint socio-cultural and artistic integration of people with special needs; - adaptation of innovative educational and scientific technologies, as well as solutions in the cross-border region; - joint creation of a new, accessible, cross-border educational offer for people of all ages; - establishing official initiatives of institutional cooperation, youth exchanges, trainings, and seminars; - developing and implementing systemic solutions and actions in order to facilitate the integration of Ukrainian children and students in Polish educational and welfare institutions; - joint initiatives to promote regular medical check-ups and updating aspects of hygiene and public health; - awareness-raising and capacity-building activities for local communities in the field of first aid in remote border areas, practical small-scale solutions, and synergies in cross-cutting healthcare and emergency situations topics.
